summary: Build AMR programme management skills with WHO-aligned tools, stewardship workflows, and dashboard practice. Enroll for practical 5-day training.
lede: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) programme management helps coordinate surveillance, stewardship, infection prevention and control, and governance. For professionals working in AMR, infection prevention and control, microbiology, quality or clinical governance, the course develops practical skills in baseline assessment, stewardship control mapping, action planning, laboratory reporting links, and performance dashboards with action tracking.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with AMR, IPC, stewardship, microbiology, quality, or clinical governance and need a more structured way to run the programme. It fits the people who translate resistance data into action, coordinate the moving parts, and report progress with credibility. AMR Programme Coordinators managing containment activities and reporting. Infection Prevention and Control Focal Points leading multimodal implementation. Antimicrobial Stewardship Leads reviewing prescribing, restriction, and feedback. Microbiology Laboratory Managers linking AST results to programme action. Public Health Officers coordinating surveillance and response activities. Clinical Governance Managers overseeing AMR performance reporting. Pharmacy Leads supporting formulary and prescribing controls. Quality Improvement Specialists tracking AMR indicators and actions. Hospital Epidemiologists analysing resistance trends and escalation needs. Infection Control Nurses implementing IPC measures and audit follow-up.
prerequisites: You should bring a basic understanding of AMR, stewardship, IPC, or microbiology reporting. A laptop is recommended for template work and dashboard exercises, and you will benefit from bringing a recent audit, surveillance summary, or programme issue from your own setting.
